title: Servers

access.title: Can't reach the server?
access.ssh: SSH with your key: ssh root@server-ip, then paste the command.
access.jump: Jump host or Tailscale: ssh -J user@jump-host root@private-ip, or use the server's Tailscale address.
access.console: Provider console: on Hetzner, Reset root password, then Console. No SSH or open port 22 needed.
access.cloudInit: At creation: paste the command in the server's cloud-init user-data and it connects on first boot.
access.outbound: After the install the agent only needs to reach this hub; port 22 can stay closed.

noContainers: No containers running (they appear a few seconds after the agent reports).
containerRemoveBody: This force-removes the container "{name}" on this server. Managed Tugra apps/databases are deleted from their own page — this is only for foreign containers. Type the name to confirm:
activityDesc: Every action taken on this server — who did what, newest first.
proxyDesc: The reverse proxy that routes traffic and manages SSL for apps with a domain.
proxyStopConfirm: Stop the proxy on this server? Every app and site it routes will go offline until it is started again.
proxyDynamicDesc: Operator-authored Traefik dynamic-config files (middlewares, TLS options, services). Each is written to the proxy and hot-reloaded. Reference a middleware from an app's domain by its name with the @file suffix (e.g. my-rate@file). An invalid file can take routes offline — the proxy logs show parse errors.
proxyDynamicEmpty: No custom dynamic configuration files yet.
proxyDynamicDeleteConfirm: Delete the dynamic configuration "{name}"? Any app referencing a middleware it defines will lose it on the next proxy reload.
selectAll: Select all servers on this page
empty: Connect your first server to start deploying apps and databases.
name: Server name (e.g. web-1)
waiting: Waiting for the agent to connect…
bulkNamesHint: {n} server(s) will be created — each gets its own install command.
bulkCreatedHint: Run each command on its server. Each shows Pending until its agent connects.
noCloudCredential: No Hetzner provider is set up for this team.
deleteServerDesc: Remove this server from Tugra. Its apps and metrics are dropped from the panel.
destroyVmHint: Tugra created this VM — leave this checked to delete it at the provider and stop billing. Uncheck to keep the VM running.
installPlainWarning: This command uses plain ws://. Commands are signed, but variables and secrets are readable on the network. Give the panel a domain (Settings, Panel domain) to encrypt it.
installPinnedNote: Encrypted. The agent trusts only this hub's own certificate (--hub-pin); no domain needed.
troubleshootHint: Check that the server can reach this hub, then read the agent logs. The command works for one hour.
noMetrics: No metrics yet — live stream starts when the agent connects.
capabilitiesDesc: What the hub is allowed to do on this server. Turn off anything you don't need — the terminal (interactive shell) is off by default on new servers.
cap_files_desc: Browse app volumes and download files through a sandboxed helper.
cap_files_write_desc: Also run a read-write helper (CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE and FOWNER, on one volume at a time) to upload, edit, rename, change permissions and delete. Requires Files.
cap_migrate: Migration helper (granted by a migration run)
cap_coolify_secrets: Read Coolify secrets (granted by the consent screen)
cap_coolify_ssh: Install agents with Coolify's SSH keys (granted by the consent screen)
cap_coolify_takeover: Take over Coolify apps in place (granted by a takeover)
cap_coolify_cleanup: Remove Coolify leftovers (granted by a cleanup)
cleanupDesc: Reclaims disk space by removing dangling image layers and build cache older than 7 days.
cleanupKeeps: Never deleted: app images (including rollback versions), stopped containers, networks and volumes. Unused anonymous volumes are removed only if “Also unused volumes” is on.
cleanupStateOffHint: Nothing is pruned on this server unless you press “Clean now”. Tick “Scheduled” and save to turn it back on.
cleanupRunsAtDisk: and whenever disk usage reaches {pct}% (at most once an hour)
cleanupDefaults: Defaults for every server: on, daily at 03:00, and also whenever disk usage reaches 80%.
cleanupCronHint: A cron expression (minute hour day month weekday) runs cleanup at a fixed time and overrides the hourly interval. Example: 0 3 * * * runs at 03:00 daily.
descriptionPlaceholder: Notes about this server (role, owner, location)…
timezoneHint: IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Istanbul. Used for the cleanup cron schedule; applies on the next cleanup save or hub restart.
cleanupThresholdHint: On top of the schedule, a cleanup also runs when this server's disk usage reaches this percentage (checked every few minutes, at most once an hour). Leave empty for the schedule only.
diskUnavailable: Disk usage unavailable (the agent is offline or the capability is not granted).
cleanConfirmVolumes: This also removes unused named volumes, which can hold data not attached to a running container. Continue?
diskWarn: Disk is filling up. Reclaim space with a cleanup under Maintenance.
diskCrit: Disk is critically full. Run a cleanup under Maintenance now.
discoverDesc: Scan this server for containers not yet managed by Tugra and adopt them as apps.
discoverOwnNote: Tugra's own containers are never listed.
noForeignContainers: No unmanaged containers found on this server.
adoptDataWarning: Adopting only renames the container. A later redeploy from Tugra recreates it and will NOT carry over its volumes or bind-mounted data — set up matching volumes first if you need the data.
adoptImageWarning: Tugra will pull this image on the next redeploy, so make sure the server can reach it (locally-built images that were never pushed will fail).
networkDesc: Set a wildcard domain to serve apps at *.your-domain, override the magic suffix, or pin a public IP. Changes regenerate this server's magic domains (apply on next deploy).
dnsProviderHint: lego provider name — e.g. cloudflare, route53, digitalocean.
dnsCredsHint: One KEY=VALUE per line (e.g. CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=…). Stored encrypted; use a least-privilege, zone-scoped token. Leave blank to keep the current credentials.
tunnelDesc: Expose this server's apps to the internet with no public IP and no port-forwarding — Tugra runs cloudflared and routes traffic through Cloudflare. Enable it per app from each app's Expose settings.
tunnelCertWarn: This server's certificate mode isn't Plain HTTP. Cloudflare terminates TLS at its edge for tunnel traffic, so set HTTPS certificates to Plain HTTP to avoid a redirect loop while the tunnel is active.
tunnelApiTokenHint: Create a token with Zone:DNS Edit, Zone:Zone Read and Account:Cloudflare Tunnel Edit. Stored encrypted; never a Global API Key.
tunnelWildcardHint: Where apps are served, e.g. apps.example.com. Defaults to the zone. A wildcard CNAME is created for it.
tunnelDisconnectConfirm: Disconnect the Cloudflare Tunnel? This stops cloudflared, deletes the tunnel and its wildcard DNS record. Apps will no longer be reachable through it.
tunnelNotConfigured: No Cloudflare Tunnel is configured for this server.
tunnelSetupFailed: Couldn't connect the tunnel. Check the API token, account ID and zone.
sealHint: This server joined with its own identity key, so the hub only trusts this exact machine.

serverScan.title: What runs on this server
serverScan.intro: See which containers, apps, sites and services run here. Nothing on the server changes.
serverScan.needsOps: You need server-ops permission to scan
serverScan.errForbidden: Scanning needs the 'bulk' capability and server-ops permission
serverScan.errUnavailable: Couldn't scan this server. Check that its agent is online.
serverScan.noDocker: Docker isn't installed on this server.
serverScan.hostOutdated: Update this server's agent to scan the host too (PM2, websites, services). Containers are shown below.
serverScan.hostFailed: Couldn't read the host this time. Containers are shown below.
serverScan.hostNoImage: This agent doesn't know its own image, so the host can't be scanned. Re-run the install command to fix it.
serverScan.exposedIntro: These ports accept connections from any address. Databases, caches and admin panels should only be reachable from this server or a private network. Tugra changes nothing here.
serverScan.exposedUnchecked: Open ports could not be checked, so no exposure warning is shown. This is not a clean result.
serverScan.exposedByAccount: Identified by the account it runs as
serverScan.exposedFirewall: Or block the port for outside addresses with ufw or your provider's firewall.

exposedFix.publish_local: Publish it on 127.0.0.1 only (use "127.0.0.1:{port}:{port}" instead of "{port}:{port}" in the container's ports).
exposedFix.bind_local: Bind the service to 127.0.0.1 in its own configuration.
exposedFix.docker_api: Remove the tcp:// listener from the Docker daemon settings, or require TLS client certificates and firewall the port.

serverScan.tugraOwnHint: Tugra's own containers (hub, agent, proxy). Managed by Tugra, nothing to move.
serverScan.pm2MoveHint: PM2 processes can move to Tugra in place: same folder, same port, no DNS or website changes.
serverScan.pm2MoveHintOwnerOnly: Only the instance owner can move PM2 processes to Tugra.

gpus.title: Detected GPUs
gpus.refreshNeedsWrite: You need server-ops permission to re-run GPU detection
gpus.driverMissing: NVIDIA GPU found but no driver loaded
gpus.runtimeMissing: Docker has no NVIDIA runtime registered. GPU containers may still work if the NVIDIA Container Toolkit is installed.
gpus.nonNvidia: Docker's --gpus flag is NVIDIA-only, so these GPUs can't be handed to containers here.
gpus.busy: Another detection is already running on this server; showing the last result.
gpus.errForbidden: GPU detection needs the 'bulk' capability and server-ops permission

acmeDns.label: Use a team DNS credential
acmeDns.noCredentials: This team has no DNS credentials yet. Add one under DNS credentials.
acmeDns.coverageVerified: Verified {date}. Make sure its token covers every zone this server serves certificates for.
acmeDns.coverageUnverified: Not verified yet. Test the credential first, and make sure its token covers every zone this server serves.
acmeDns.readOnly: This credential is read-only, so it cannot create the DNS-01 challenge records.
acmeDns.tokenCopied: The token is copied to this server when you save. If you rotate the credential later, the server keeps the old token until you re-apply it.
acmeDns.reapplyHint: Save first to switch credentials; re-apply only refreshes the one already in use.

teamMoveDesc: Choose which team owns this server.
teamMoveNoTargets: You have no other team to move this server to.
teamMoveSafe: The agent stays connected and nothing is reinstalled.
teamMoveBlocked: This server still has resources that belong to {team}. Move or remove them first.
teamMoveBlockedRetry: Something new appeared on this server. Move or remove it first.
teamMoveMoreKeeps: Settings, metrics, traffic and history stay with the server.
teamMoveMoreMonitor: Its default disk monitor moves with it.
teamMoveDetachCloud: The cloud provider link ({name}) is removed. Link a provider key of the new team to restore power and rescue actions.
teamMoveDetachCloudUnnamed: The cloud provider link is removed. Link a provider key of the new team to restore power and rescue actions.
teamMoveDetachDns: The DNS credential link ({name}) is cleared.
teamMoveDetachDnsUnnamed: The DNS credential link is cleared.
teamMoveDetachDnsSecret: The copied DNS token is deleted and wildcard certificates switch to HTTP. Add a DNS credential of the new team to restore them.
teamMoveDetachChannels: Alerts from its default disk monitor stop going to the old team's channels.
teamMoveOpenShells: Open terminals on this server are closed.
teamMoveBlocker_build_server: Apps that build on this server
teamMoveBlocker_app_move: App moves in progress or awaiting cleanup
teamMoveBlocker_reboot: A reboot in progress or scheduled
quickTerminalOff: Terminal is off for this server

bulkCaps.title: Access for {n} selected
bulkCaps.hint: Turn opt-in features on or off. Everything below is listed before you confirm.
bulkCaps.desc_terminal: Opens a root shell on the server.
bulkCaps.desc_files_write: Upload, edit and delete app files. Needs Files.
bulkCaps.desc_swarm: Let the server join a Docker Swarm.

teamMoveBulk.title: Move {n} servers to another team
teamMoveBulk.hint: Each server is checked on its own. Servers that still hold the old team's apps or databases stay where they are.
teamMoveBulk.status_blocked: Stays: old team's resources on it

nameHint: Leave it blank and the server's own hostname is used. You can rename it later.
ipUnknownHint: Not detected. Enter it under Network.
ipPinFailed: Could not set the main address.
agentFleetBehind: {n}/{total} agents are on an older version
agentFleetAuto: They are updating one by one.
agentFleetWaitingHub: The hub updates first, then the agents follow.
agentFleetManual: Update them all in one click, or turn on automatic updates and the hub keeps every agent current.
agentFleetNone: Nothing could be updated right now.
agentFleetHubBehind: Update the hub first. Agents never run ahead of it.
capOffHint: {name} off · turn it on in Access (select servers) or the server's Settings
adoptComposeHint: Containers started by docker compose are adopted as a whole stack, from the first container of the project. Leave them running; they keep working.
stackAdoptOnFirst: Adopt the whole {project} stack from its first container.
stackNeedsAdmin: Only team owners and admins can adopt a compose stack.
stackModalDesc: Tugra takes over this docker compose project where it is. Nothing is renamed, stopped or recreated.
stackVolumes: {n} named volumes stay exactly where they are.
stackNoRecreate: Future deploys run docker compose with the same project name and these same files, so unchanged services keep running. If the compose version differs from the one that started them, compose may still recreate a service once.
stackFilesStay: The files stay on the server and are never copied or rewritten: edit them there. Domains and environment variables set in Tugra don't apply to an adopted stack. Deleting the app only unregisters it.

stackRefusal.tugra: This project is part of Tugra and can't be adopted.
stackRefusal.managed: Coolify or Dokploy runs this project. Move it with that platform's import instead.
stackRefusal.no_config: This project doesn't record its working directory and compose files, so Tugra couldn't run it later.
stackRefusal.unsafe_path: This project lives in a place Tugra can't mount safely (a system directory, or spaces or special characters in the path).
stackRefusal.bad_name: This project's name can't be used.
stackRefusal.name_clash: Another container's name starts with this project's name, so the two can't be told apart. Rename the project first.

adoptManagedHint: {platform} runs this container. The {platform} import moves it together with its settings, domains and data.

pm2Move.title: Move PM2 processes to Tugra
pm2Move.intro: Each process keeps running from its own folder, on the same port, with the same environment and user. Your web server and DNS are not touched.
pm2Move.errOwner: Only the instance owner can do this.
pm2Move.errForbidden: Needs server-ops permission and the 'patch' and 'deploy' capabilities on this server.
pm2Move.errOutdated: Update this server's agent to read its PM2 processes.
pm2Move.errUnavailable: Couldn't read the PM2 processes. Check that the agent is online.
pm2Move.errBusy: A move is already running on this server.
pm2Move.truncated: Only the first processes are shown.

reason.not-running: It isn't running in PM2. Start it first.
reason.cluster-instances: It runs several instances in cluster mode. That isn't moved yet.
reason.duplicate-name: Several PM2 entries share this name.
reason.name-unsafe: The name can't be used safely with PM2 commands.
reason.interpreter: It runs with {interpreter}, which isn't Node.
reason.script-outside: The script is outside its working folder.
reason.no-cwd: No working folder is saved for it.
reason.cwd-unsafe: Its working folder is too broad or protected to share with a container.
reason.args-unsafe: Its start arguments can't be carried over exactly.

warning.root: Runs as root, same as in PM2 today.
warning.node-eol: This Node version is past end of life. It keeps working, but plan an upgrade.
warning.no-port: No port is known, so the check only confirms it keeps running.
warning.owner-differs: The folder belongs to a different user than the process.
warning.cluster-single: Cluster mode with one instance runs as a single process.
warning.node-guessed: This Node version comes from the project files (.nvmrc or package.json), not from what PM2 ran. Confirm it before moving.
warning.shared-env: Your team has {n} shared variables. Tugra adds them to every app, so this one may get up to {n} variables PM2 never had (its own variables win).

pm2Move.probeHint: For example /health. After the port opens, this path must answer.

confirm.title: Review before moving
confirm.intro: Each selected process is moved one after the other. This is what happens to each:
confirm.s1: The Node image is downloaded first, while the process keeps running.
confirm.s2: The process is stopped in PM2. Downtime is a few seconds, until the new container is listening.
confirm.s3: It starts as a Tugra container on the host network: same port, same folder (read and write), same user, same environment, restarts automatically.
confirm.s4: Tugra checks that it keeps running and that the port answers.
confirm.s5: If it's healthy, it's removed from PM2. If anything fails, the container is removed and the process is restarted in PM2 exactly as it was.
confirm.s6: Websites and DNS stay as they are.
confirm.privilege: The new apps run with host networking and read-write access to their own folder. This is recorded in the audit log.
confirm.s7: Each move is checked once more right before it runs. If the process or its saved environment changed since this preview, it is skipped.

job.title: Moving…
job.scanAgain: Scan the server again to refresh this list.
job.pm2Left: Moved, but it couldn't be removed from PM2. Delete the stopped entry with pm2 delete, then pm2 save.

status.rolled_back: Rolled back, PM2 is running it again
status.plan_changed: Not moved, it changed since the preview
status.rollback_failed: Failed and PM2 could not be restarted. Check it now.

code.pull_failed: The Node image couldn't be downloaded.
code.port_busy: Something else still holds the port.
code.container_exited: The container stopped or kept restarting.
code.http_failed: The health check path didn't answer properly.
code.host_unavailable: The server's host helper isn't available.
code.nobin: The pm2 program wasn't found for this account.
code.norunuser: The runuser tool is missing on the host.
code.recovered: Recovered after losing contact with the server.
code.gone: It is neither in PM2 nor running. Check it now.
code.capability: A required capability is turned off for this server.
code.invalid: It can't be carried over exactly.
code.changed: The process or its environment changed.
code.busy: Another move of this process is still running.

pm2Move.errTooLarge: This process's saved environment is too large to move.
pm2Move.probeInvalid: Start with / and use only letters, numbers and . _ ~ - / (no spaces or ?).
pm2Move.envNote: The environment comes from PM2's saved process list (pm2 save). A variable changed with pm2 restart --update-env and never saved isn't included. Save PM2 first if you did that.

scanBulk.hint: See what runs on {n} selected servers (read-only).
scanBulk.none: Select online servers you can operate to scan them.
scanBulk.partial: Scanned {ok} servers, {failed} failed. Open a server to see why.

cta.blockPending: Not connected yet. Finish the agent install on this server first.
cta.blockOffline: This server is offline. Bring its agent back online first.
cta.blockNoWrite: You can view this server but not change it. Ask a team owner or admin.
cta.blockCapability: Needs the {caps} capability on this server.
cta.platformNeeds: Their settings are stored in {platform}, not on this server. To move them you need a {platform} API token.
cta.platformMore: The repository, variables, domains and build settings live in {platform}'s own database. The token needs read and read:sensitive. Without a token, add the server that runs {platform} to Tugra, then use Read this {platform}. That is a preview only; nothing moves from there.
cta.platformMoreDokploy: The repository, variables, domains and build settings live in Dokploy's own database. The key needs an owner or admin account. Paste it into the Dokploy import.
cta.infraStays: {platform} itself ({n} containers) stays where it is. It is not moved.
cta.infraStaysOne: {platform} itself (1 container) stays where it is. It is not moved.
cta.runsCoolifyRead: To bring its apps over, read this Coolify first (a preview), or use an API token.
cta.swarm_one: 1 container is a Swarm service, often a Dokploy app. It can't be adopted on its own.
cta.swarm_other: {n} containers are Swarm services, often Dokploy apps. They can't be adopted on their own.
cta.stacks_one: 1 compose stack can be adopted as one app (team owners and admins).
cta.stacks_other: {n} compose stacks can be adopted as one app each (team owners and admins).
cta.standalone_one: 1 container can be adopted as a Tugra app.
cta.standalone_other: {n} containers can be adopted as Tugra apps.
cta.sitesStay: Websites on nginx, Apache or CloudPanel stay where they are. Tugra doesn't move them; they keep running next to it.
cta.swarmRefused: This container is a Swarm service (often Dokploy). Move it with the Dokploy import.
cta.needsImport: Needs the {platform} import and an API token.
cta.noOtherServer: There is no other server in this team.
